extracted.intended_audience: journal press officers, science communicators, and editors
extracted.subtask_description: A concise set of empirically derived criteria predicting whether a journal article will be picked up by mainstream newspapers; aimed at press officers and publishers to increase pickup probability. Focuses on release existence, venue prestige, timing/embargo, language, topic fit, visuals, expert quotes, and distribution coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-press-release existence
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the journal itself, or the publishing institution, issued a press release for the article? (Without this, newspaper pickup is rare.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: de Semir et al. identify press-release existence as the primary predictor of newspaper coverage: articles with a press release were much more likely to be covered. Practical implication: if you want newspaper pickup, issue a press release; within the press-released set, other factors (see below) act as secondary predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal prestige (BMJ / Lancet / Science / Nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases from these high-impact venues amplify pickup; sub-rubric for issuers: identify the highest-impact venue the result legitimately fits and place there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-impact journals confer greater pickup probability. Where possible, position results in the most prestigious, appropriate outlet; prominence of the issuing journal is a multiplier on pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-language translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release exist in the target country's language, or is the headline phrased so it survives a wire translator?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide releases in local languages for non-English outlets or craft headlines and lede sentences that translate cleanly over wires. Releases that are language-appropriate or wire-resilient are more likely to be picked up by foreign papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-zone embargo coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the embargo lift at a time-of-day workable in the target outlet's edition cycle? European journal embargo lifts at a US-friendly hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate embargo times so the release becomes available during the news outlet's working hours and production cycles (e.g., US-friendly hours for US papers). Poorly timed embargoes reduce practical pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain topics (cardiovascular, oncology, infectious disease) dominate press-release-driven coverage. Releases pegged to a topic the receiving newspapers are currently covering compound their pickup advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match releases to subjects that are both high-interest to newspapers and currently in the news cycle. Topic choice matters: some fields attract disproportionately more coverage; topical alignment with current events increases pickup probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page-photo opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Print papers prefer releases with at least one print-quality image of either the lead author or a representative subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply at least one high-resolution, print-ready image (author portrait or representative subject) to increase the chance of prominent placement. Visual assets lower editors' production costs and raise placement likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent-comment pre-supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases that include a comment from an independent expert at another institution reduce the journalist's verification cost and increase pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include or arrange for an independent external comment to be available in the release. Independent quotes reduce reporters' need to find external verification and make the story easier and more credible to run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent-day distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinated same-day distribution to multiple international wires increases pickup correlation across newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute the release to multiple outlets/wires on the same day to amplify simultaneous pickup across markets. Synchronized international distribution raises the odds of cross-national coverage.
